content.text: A covering-array stress case can make every positive four-atom clause eligible simultaneously (4,845 members in one probe class), which exercises member accounting and class-wide query evaluation rather than just representatives. I’m using that to check enumeration and aggregation under a substantially larger result.

arguments.command:
cat > /workspace/devtests/stress_clauses.py <<'PY'
import itertools,json,subprocess,time
n=20
schema=[{'name':f'f{i}','type':'FLAG'} for i in range(n)]
atoms=[{'cmp':'eq','left':{'field':f'f{i}','at':0},'right':{'const':True,'type':'FLAG'}} for i in range(n)]
rows=[]
for zeros in itertools.combinations(range(n),3):
 z=set(zeros);rows.append({'t':len(rows),'values':[i not in z for i in range(n)]})
# Several query patterns expose all-false, mixed, and all-true class behavior.
qrows=[{'t':0,'values':[False]*n},{'t':1,'values':[True]*n}]
for i in range(10):qrows.append({'t':i+2,'values':[j==i for j in range(n)]})
req={'version':1,'schema':schema,'window':1,'atoms':atoms,'policy':{'max_width':4,'min_support':1,'min_witness':1},'train':[{'id':'train','source':'s','rows':rows}], 'probes':[{'id':'probe','source':'p','rows':[{'t':0,'values':[False]*n}]}], 'queries':[{'id':'query','source':'q','rows':qrows}]}
data=json.dumps(req,separators=(',',':')).encode();t=time.time();p=subprocess.run(['/app/submission/run.sh'],input=data,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.PIPE,timeout=170);dt=time.time()-t
print('wall',dt,'input',len(data),'output',len(p.stdout),'return',p.returncode,'stderr',p.stderr[:500]);o=json.loads(p.stdout);print('classes',len(o['classes']),'total members',sum(c['members'] for c in o['classes']));print('first classes',o['classes'][:3]);print('queries',o['queries'])
assert any(c['members']>=4845 for c in o['classes'])
open('/workspace/devtests/stress_clauses.out','wb').write(p.stdout)
PY
python3 /workspace/devtests/stress_clauses.py
